name: Cinematic bass FX bed: WT+sub through stacked distortion/compression, then pitch-bend downer
goal: Build a full cinematic bass/impact bed by pitching a wavetable osc down an octave with subtle bend-warp and width, stacking multiple distortions and compressors so the WT choice matters less than the grind, pushing a sine sub through the same FX, adding early-chain filter/EQ movement into the grit, then reusing the patch for braams/bends/downers via one-shot pitch curves and asymmetric filter envelopes.

source.title: How To Sound Design Cinematic Basses and Subdrops

prerequisites: Wavetable synth with warp/bend, unison width, FX rack (distortion, compressor, filter), pitch envelope/curves

outputs.name: cinematic_bass_fx
outputs.description: Distorted cinematic bass reusable for bends and downers

constraints: Portable signal-flow recipe for Web Audio / Traveler-inspired / any hybrid synth with comparable modules; not affiliated with any vendor.
Do not copy proprietary factory preset banks, wavetable file names, or sample packs; use original/free waves or generic shapes.
Steps and numeric values are grounded only in the YouTube Show-transcript text; approximate where the speaker gestured without stating a number.
Do not copy named factory WT/preset labels from the video; pick any original/free complex table or basic shapes plus bend.
Delta vs existing braam skill: emphasis on heavy serial distortion/compression bed + sub-through-FX and downer filter curves, not the sine+dual-saw formant braam recipe.

steps.action: Init WT osc; transpose −12 st. Apply a bend-style warp in small amounts to soften robotic digital WT character. Add modest unison width with reduced detune so it is wide but not chorus-wobbly.

Stack several distortions and compressors in series. The more extreme the stack, the less the specific WT matters. Use some compressors to bring high-end back; disable multiband modes if the tone goes boxy.
steps.expect: Dense, aggressive bass bed dominated by grit

steps.action: Place a filter or EQ early in the FX chain and modulate a morph/cutoff with one slow LFO plus a second LFO (different rate, limited depth) so movement is smashed into the distortion.

Add a second oscillator +12 st with fewer unison voices for air. Keep a sine sub in the patch and intentionally run it through the same FX — bypassing FX shows how much the sub colors the grind; tweak sub pitch for large timbral changes.
steps.expect: Sub+FX interaction is audible; octave layer adds presence

steps.action: Post: more compression/saturation (soft-clip/inflator-style with low drive), limiter, enable legato/glide. For braams/bends draw a one-shot pitch curve (e.g. 2 bars). For downers invert the pitch gesture and automate filter cutoff with a fast-then-slow asymmetric curve over ~2 bars, optionally keeping lows less affected.
steps.expect: Same bed becomes bend, braam-ish hit, or downer via curves only

verification: Bypassing the distortion stack reveals a quieter cleaner WT+sub; engaging it massively increases density
Pitch one-shot produces a bend/braam gesture; opposite curve + filter produces a downer
Sub pitch changes alter the distorted timbre even when WT is unchanged
